newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs stalled by weather - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs stalled by weather - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog trade was stalled by harsh winter weather, with no hogs reportedly trading at buying stations in Illinois and Indiana and very few moving to interior Iowa and southern Minnesota stations and plants.

Strong winds and blowing snow were blocking rural roads and producing wind chill readings of -45 Fahrenheit in southern Minnesota and -20 to -40 F in Iowa, Illinois and Indiana. Wind chills overnight in southern Minnesota were -60 to -70 F, sources there said.
Ohio buyers said producers were able to move a few hogs that were fetching steady prices at $50.50 to $51.50 in the country and $52.50 to $53.00 at plants.
Treacherous road conditions throughout the Corn Belt sharply reduced livestock movement, as did the dangerous wind chill readings, dealers said.
"People just are not in the mood to move hogs," said one central Iowa hog buyer.
Light sales were reported steady to $0.50 higher at interior Iowa/southern Minnesota points, with $52.50-$453.50 paid in the country and $53.50-$54.50 at plants.
There were reports of producers asking $60.00 for hogs, but packers were passing, the dealers said.
